bottom_line: Prices are still rising too fast, so the Fed (the people who set interest rates) is widely expected to raise rates again in December. That makes borrowing more expensive, and it is the reason stocks have been so shaky this month.

stories.title: Fed leaning toward another rate hike
stories.real: Inflation hit a 3-year high, and many economists expect the Fed to raise rates by 25 bps (basis points, small steps of interest) in December. Some analysts warn markets could crack before the Dec. 9 decision, and economists are split on it.
stories.you: Credit cards, car loans and other borrowing would likely get more expensive if the Fed hikes.

stories.title: Trump calls GDP numbers fake
stories.real: The government's third-quarter GDP number, which measures the size of the economy, was revised much higher. President Trump called it a 'record setting error' and 'fake' and demanded an investigation of the Commerce Department.
stories.you: When people stop trusting official economic numbers, it gets harder for everyone, including the Fed, to know what's really going on.

stories.title: Everyday costs still squeezing families
stories.real: Rising inflation is squeezing shoppers this holiday season. The average new car price hit a record $51,109 in October, according to Kelley Blue Book. The number of Amazon workers on food stamps has tripled.
stories.you: Your paycheck may not stretch as far this holiday season, so big purchases need extra care.
